# API Developer Portal

> A developer portal for discovering, subscribing to, and integrating with APIs programmatically.
> Agents can browse the full API catalog, fetch OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications, subscribe to APIs,
> and generate credentials — either through MCP tool calls or REST JSON endpoints.

> **IMPORTANT: All REST API requests MUST include the `Accept: application/json` header.**
> Without this header, the portal returns HTML pages intended for browsers — not machine-readable
> JSON. Every endpoint listed below requires `Accept: application/json` to return structured data.

## IMPORTANT: The Portal Is a Setup Tool — Not a Runtime Dependency

**Use the portal only during the setup/provisioning phase** — to discover an API, subscribe to it,
and obtain credentials. Once you have the target API's base URL and credentials, your application
should call the target API directly. The portal must NOT appear in your final application.

**Correct model:**

  1. Agent uses the portal → discovers the API, fetches its OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification
    and fetches Arazzo specification.
  2. Agent builds the integration code using the spec and Arazzo spec: HTTP client, request/response
     models, error handling, etc. Use placeholder environment variables for credentials
     (e.g. API_BASE_URL, API_KEY) — do NOT block on obtaining real credentials.
  3. Agent returns to the portal → creates an app, subscribes (if required), generates credentials.
  4. Agent stores the resulting base URL + credentials in the application's config (e.g. .env file)
     and verifies the integration works end-to-end.

  Build first, provision later: Use the API spec to write integration code.
  If a request fails when trying to generate credentials with 401, instruct the user to log in to the portal,
  create an app, subscribe to the API (if needed), and generate an API Key.

**Things to avoid in the application you build:**

- Do NOT create a portal/devportal client class in the application.
- Do NOT call portal endpoints at application startup, in health checks, or at request time.
- Do NOT expose portal routes (e.g. /api/portal/...) to end users of the application.
- Do NOT store portal URLs or portal bearer tokens in the application's runtime config.

The portal is an agent-facing provisioning tool. End users of the application you build have no
business interacting with the portal. Treat it the same way you treat a CI pipeline or a
one-time database migration: useful during setup, invisible at runtime.

## Quick Start for MCP-Capable Agents (Recommended)

If your agent speaks MCP, connect directly — no URL fetching needed:

  POST {host}/{orgName}/mcp
  Transport: Streamable HTTP

Replace {orgName} with the organisation name (first path segment of any portal URL).
Once connected, call tools/list to see everything available.

Tools available through MCP:
  Discovery (no auth): list_apis, get_api_details, get_api_specification,
                       list_mcp_servers, get_mcp_server_details, list_subscription_plans
  Applications (auth): create_application, list_applications, delete_application
  Subscriptions (auth): subscribe_to_api, list_subscriptions, unsubscribe
  Keys (auth):          generate_api_key, list_api_keys, revoke_api_key

The MCP server also exposes:
  Resources: per-API specs, documentation pages, MCP server schemas,
             portal integration guide, error reference, auth guide, access level rules
  Prompts:   discover_and_subscribe, integrate_api, explain_access_levels, troubleshoot_error

---

## Getting Started (REST fallback — for agents that do not speak MCP)

The portal is organised by organisation (org). Each org has its own API catalog.
To get started, you need to know the org name — then fetch its discovery document.

### Step 1 — Find the org name

If the user mentioned an org name explicitly (e.g. "use the acme org") or gave you a
portal URL (e.g. {host}/acme/views/default/apis), extract the org name from that.
The org name is the first path segment after the portal host.
Only ask the user for the org name if it is genuinely unknown from context.

### Step 2 — Fetch the per-org discovery document

  {host}/{orgName}/agent.json
  (replace {orgName} with the org name you found in step 1)

This returns:
- The MCP endpoint URL for this org (recommended connection method)
- Concrete, ready-to-call REST URLs for all capabilities (no further substitution needed)
- A workflows array pointing to the Arazzo integration workflow — a machine-executable
  step-by-step guide with explicit branching, input/output mappings, and human approval gates

## Integration Workflows (Arazzo)

Each workflow phase has its own file — fetch only what you need for your current step.

  Phase 1 — Discovery (no auth):
    {host}/workflows/discover-api.arazzo.yaml
    Use this standalone for research or API selection — it stops after recommending
    the best match and generates no credentials. Also the first step of a full integration.

  Phase 2 — Build integration code (no file needed):
    Use the spec from Phase 1 to write your HTTP client, request/response models,
    and error handling with placeholder env vars (API_BASE_URL, API_KEY).
    Use the sandbox endpoint if available, otherwise production.
    Build BEFORE requesting credentials — do not wait for provisioning.

  Phase 3 — Generate credentials (auth required, fetch ONE based on gateway):
    {host}/workflows/generate-wso2-key.arazzo.yaml          (gateway_vendor == "wso2/api-platform")
    {host}/workflows/generate-cloud-api-key.arazzo.yaml     (other gateways + api_key scheme)
    {host}/workflows/generate-oauth2-credentials.arazzo.yaml (other gateways + oauth2 scheme)

  Orchestrator (references all phases):
    {host}/workflows/integrate-api.arazzo.yaml

### Human approval gates

Two points in the workflow require you to pause and confirm with the operator:

  1. Before generating credentials — unless the operator has explicitly requested it,
     pause at the credential-generation step. Show the API name and available plans,
     then ask: "Do you want me to generate credentials for <apiName>? [yes / no]"
     Proceed only on confirmation.

  2. Before subscribing to an API — subscribing creates a formal relationship and may
     incur billing charges. Always confirm with the operator before proceeding,
     even if credential generation was already approved.

## REST API Catalog

{viewName} defaults to `default` when not specified by the user.

Call these endpoints in order — each step depends on the previous one:

### 1. List APIs

  GET {host}/{orgName}/views/{viewName}/apis
  GET {host}/{orgName}/views/{viewName}/apis?query=payment   (keyword search)
  Accept: application/json

Returns a list of APIs with summary info. Use this to find candidate `apiHandle` values.

### 2. Get API Details

  GET {host}/{orgName}/views/{viewName}/api/{apiHandle}
  Accept: application/json

Returns full detail for a single API. Key fields to check:
  agent_access.level      — full | human_approval | hidden (see Agent Access Levels below)
  agent_access.reason     — explanation shown to the operator when approval is required
  gateway_vendor          — determines which credential workflow to use (see Integration Workflows above)
  subscription_required   — if true, the agent must subscribe before generating credentials
  recommended_base_url    — the target API's base URL; use this in your integration code
  subscription_plans      — available plans and their costs; show to operator before subscribing
  endpoints               - base url of the API

### 3. Fetch API Specification

  GET {host}/{orgName}/views/{viewName}/api/{apiHandle}/docs/specification
  Accept: application/json

Returns the raw OpenAPI / AsyncAPI / GraphQL spec. Read the `securitySchemes` section —
it determines which credential workflow to use alongside `gateway_vendor`.

### 4. Fetch API Usage Workflow (if available)

  GET {host}/{orgName}/views/{viewName}/api/{apiHandle}/docs/workflow
  Accept: application/json

Only fetch this when the detail or spec response indicates it is available
(`_api_usage_workflow_available: true` / `_api_usage_workflow_link` present).

This describes how the API's own operations connect for real-world use cases —
the correct sequence of calls, inputs/outputs between steps, and supported scenarios.
Use it as the blueprint for building your integration code.

Note: This is different from the portal integration workflows (listed above under
"Integration Workflows"), which describe how to interact with this developer portal.

## MCP Servers Catalog

List available MCP servers (JSON):
  {host}/{orgName}/views/{viewName}/mcps
  Accept: application/json

## Agent Access Levels

Each API declares an agent_access level in its JSON response and as MCP tool output:
  full            — agent can discover, read, subscribe, and invoke freely
  human_approval  — The agent must obtain explicit approval from its human operator 
                    before using the API, subscribing, or generating credentials.
  hidden          — not visible to agents at all

## Authentication

Discovery tools and endpoints require no authentication.
Subscription, application, and key management require a bearer token.
